driver_concrete: The winter respiratory wave moves north through a hospital cooperative's three regions: in every winter on the capacity census it reaches the eight northern Michigan hospitals about four weeks after Central (Tennessee, Kentucky and West Virginia), while Central's gap behind the Southeast (Georgia and South Carolina) and the wave's calendar timing move by weeks; this winter the Southeast surged in late November and Central in mid-December, so the four weeks from Monday 4 January 2027 hold none of the sixteen southern hospitals' surge days and the whole of the North's, whose eight hospitals join the pool this winter and whose wave fell in February or March in every earlier winter; the block is the North's own per-wave surge-day draw at its surge plans' agency staffing, 600 shifts.
stump: Averaging the closed winters' January block draws, the sixteen southern members' surge nights in those four weeks at their surge plans' agency staffing with the North's none, files 2,450 shifts; the step that lands it there is reading January by the calendar when the respiratory wave's timing moves by weeks from winter to winter, and the analyst who times the North from the Southeast instead, whose lead over the North moved by two weeks or more, puts its wave partly before the block; the North follows Central by about four weeks, and Central's spells began 9 to 17 December, so this January holds the North's whole wave and none of the south's: 600 shifts.

domain_test: The deciding quantity is each region's January surge staffing demand, forecast the way health-system capacity planners forecast a winter surge: by where each region's respiratory wave falls in the window, timed from the region it follows by the lag past winters show, and turned into agency shifts through each hospital's surge unit staffing; with another field's nouns (megawatt-hours, crew hours) there is no epidemic moving north from region to region at a lag of weeks, no surge plan opening agency-staffed beds and no reason one region's whole demand should fall in a window it has never touched.
